title: AgentFlow Workflow Graph (DSL v1)
description: JSON Schema for the declarative, typed DAG persisted as workflow_definition_versions.graph_json (ADR-005). It fixes the shape of a v1 workflow graph: a schemaVersion, an ordered list of typed nodes and the edges that order them. The allowed node types are the closed set from docs/domain-glossary.md and ADR-005 (RETRIEVE_CONTEXT, LLM_PLAN, TOOL_CALL, HUMAN_APPROVAL, LLM_EVALUATE, FINALIZE). Node ids, edge endpoints and input references must name existing nodes, the graph must be acyclic and free of dangling, duplicate or self-referencing edges, and every node id must be unique. Those topology rules are not expressible in portable JSON Schema and are enforced by the workflowdefinition DSL validator (S05-05, S05-06, S05-07); this schema enforces everything it can: the required fields, the closed node-type set, field shapes and patterns, and the node/edge size limits below. Input/output wiring is optional data mapping; edges express execution order.

schemaVersion.description: The DSL schema version this graph conforms to. Only 1.0.0 is defined by this file; any other value is rejected so an unknown version yields a controlled validation error (S05-04).

nodes.description: The ordered steps of the graph. At least one node is required (an empty graph is not a runnable workflow); capped at 200 to bound graph size and cost (S05-03, S05-06).

edges.description: Execution-order edges between node ids. May be empty for a single-node graph; capped at 1000 (S05-03).

nodeType.description: The closed set of allowed node types (docs/domain-glossary.md, ADR-005). The WorkflowNodeTypeRegistry (S05-07) is the closed authority for this set going forward; the DSL validator rejects any node whose type is not in it before a version is persisted, so a client/LLM cannot register its own executable type.

nodeId.description: A stable, non-blank identifier that must be unique across the graph. Uniqueness is enforced by the DSL validator (S05-05), not by this schema (JSON Schema cannot express cross-item uniqueness portably).

config.description: Free-form, per-step parameters. Treated as untrusted DATA, never executed (invariant 7).

input.description: Optional mapping of an input name to a literal string or to another node's output. Wire a downstream input to an upstream output here.

output.description: Optional declaration of this node's named outputs. Downstream inputs reference them via a {node, output} reference.

node.description: A single typed step in the graph.

edge.description: An execution-order edge from the 'from' node to the 'to' node. Self-references, dangling endpoints and duplicate edges are rejected by the DSL validator (S05-05, S05-06), not by this schema.

reference.description: An input value: either a literal string or a reference to another node's output. The referenced node id must exist and expose that output; that linkage is checked by the DSL validator (S05-05), not by this schema.
